Truncation Checker

Catch files that got clipped mid-write.
SKILL · RUNS AUTOMATICALLY WHEN IT APPLIES

What it does

Runs a token-minimal, workspace-wide sweep for files that were truncated mid-write - clipped before the write finished. It is the detection backstop to the write-time prevention sweep: where prevention tries to stop a bad write from landing, this skill finds the ones that slipped through and tells you exactly which files need attention.

What it catches

  • Mid-word tails - text that stops abruptly partway through a word or sentence.
  • Missing structural closers - no </html>, an unterminated JSON object/array, or an incomplete Python file.
  • Empty files that should have content.
  • Trailing NUL padding left behind by an interrupted write.

Auto-fix vs. report

It auto-fixes the lossless case on its own: trailing NUL padding is stripped, since no real content is lost. Lossy truncation - where actual content was cut off and cannot be recovered - is never silently patched, because guessing at the missing text is how a corrupt file becomes a plausible-looking wrong one.

Instead, each flagged file gets a one-click-copy handoff block addressed to The Architect: the file path, what was detected, and the instruction to rebuild the missing tail from source. You paste it and the repair happens as a deliberate, sourced rewrite rather than a hand-patch you have to reconstruct from memory.

A clean scan returns a single line. No findings means one all-clear, not a report full of green checkmarks - so a run with something in it is impossible to skim past.

How it runs

It wraps the root verify-write.py --scan engine. There is no daily scheduled scan. The truncation-daily-scan task was retired 2026-08-10; the recurring sweep is now Check 15 of the System Monitor weekly health check (Mondays), which runs the same engine read-only - no --fix-nulls - because System Monitor is read-only by hard rule. This skill is on-demand only, and it is the write-capable path: since the weekly sweep cannot repair, this skill is now the only thing that strips NUL padding. Run it on demand, or when the Monday report flags Check 15.

When to use it

After a large batch of writes, after an interrupted or crashed session, or whenever a file looks like it ends in the wrong place. Because nothing repairs NUL padding on a schedule any more, also run it whenever the Monday Check 15 report flags something - that report detects, it does not fix.

How to trigger it

"run a truncation scan"

"check for truncated files"

"did anything get clipped mid-write"

Requirements

What this skill needs in order to run. Added 2026-08-20.

Skills - None.

Connectors / MCP servers - None. Note it explicitly does not call present_files and never emits an HTML report - the handoff code block is its only output.

Folder access - Read access to the workspace being swept, and write access only for the lossless repair it performs.

KB modules / context files - None.

Repos - None.

If something is missing - An unreadable scan root is LOUD and reported as a literal condition rather than an all-clear. The severe SILENT case is what the skill exists for: NUL padding and clipped tails pass every ordinary check, and the recurring weekly sweep is read-only, so nothing repairs padding on a schedule. This on-demand run is the only path that repairs it. Lossy truncation is never invented back.
